state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's start by identifying the shapes in the net. The circle represents the base, and the sector represents a side. To visualize this as a 3D shape, imagine folding the sides up to form a cone. Can you picture how the net corresponds to a cone now?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so the circle folds up to make the pointy bit at the top? I think I see it now - the sector wraps around the side... but I'm still a bit confused about how the flat sector actually becomes the curved side when you fold it up?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's think about how the flat sector can transform into a curved side. When you fold the sector along the curved edge, it forms the curved surface of the cone. Can you visualize how the flat shape transforms into the curved side of the cone now?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Yeah, I think I'm getting it a bit more now... so the curved edge of the sector is like the pointy tip of the cone, and when you roll it up the straight edges of the sector meet together? But I'm still not really sure why the sector becomes curved when it folds - like, doesn't it stay flat?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher fails to address the student's deepening confusion about how flat shapes become curved surfaces, provides mathematically incorrect explanations (claiming the circle becomes the pointy bit, misidentifying which edge is which), and the student's understanding deteriorates rather than improves across the dialogue.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher relies heavily on questioning and asking the student to visualize rather than directly explaining with worked examples or providing clear, comprehensive explanations as the traditional strategy requires.
